I will agree that the DSM suffers from "see a bunch of behaviors and slap a name on it" but I believe there is a lot of brain chemistry that we do understand. We know how serotonin affects behavior, and how amphetamines affect the amount of serotonin in the brain. The big problem is that there aren't bright lines in behaviors - bipolar vs. chronic depression vs. ADD are actually just a big smear of symptoms that psychiatrists drew lines through to mark off areas. From symptomatic analysis it's like flu vs. a cold vs. pneumonia, and a patient comes in complaining of cough, sore throat, and fever.

The difference there is that at the causation level those three have distinct causes. With the psychiatric "things" this isn't true. One person with "ADD" may have a serotonin imbalance, while another may just have shitty work habits. And the serious problem here is that amphetamines always help everyone, so prescribing adderall always solves the problem, at least superficially.

My point is that there are brain chemistry imbalances and they can be treated with pharmaceuticals. But it's not like diseases where there's always a distinct causal relationship and cure.

As a related note, there are also some "disorders" (I hate that word) where the treatment is "help the patient understand what they're doing wrong and how to deal with it"
